title: How America’s Military Shaped the Nation’s History and Evolved Over 250 Years
gist: Short CNAS video page pointing to a PBS segment (Judy Woodruff's 'Crossroads: America at 250') on how the U.S. military shaped national history; the core point is that as the military's reach has grown, fewer Americans serve in uniform. Content is a teaser only.

insights.claim: Over 250 years the U.S. military has helped shape the nation's history, from the fight for independence to its emergence as the world's leading military power.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Context framing only; little direct market signal.

insights.claim: As the U.S. military's reach has grown, fewer Americans are serving in uniform, raising questions about what that means for the country.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: A narrowing recruitment base is a structural constraint on force size and a tailwind for automation/unmanned systems in defense.
insights.quote: But as the military's reach has grown, fewer Americans are serving in uniform.

insights.claim: Judy Woodruff examines the military's evolution and declining participation in her PBS series Crossroads: America at 250.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Signals mainstream attention to civil-military gap around the U.S. 250th anniversary.
